subject: NobleCare: post-call recap & VPC hosting constraints
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Park <epark@noblecare.health>; Tom Reyes <t.reyes@noblecare.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: NobleCare call — recap, constraints, and proposed next steps

Hi Emily & Tom,

Thanks again for a tight, productive call earlier — appreciated the clarity on regulatory drivers and the timeline. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned, plus the concrete next steps we discussed.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary constraint: data residency + auditability for clinical records (must remain in EU region and be available for 7 years for audit).
- Regulatory driver: national healthcare regulator requires air-gapped or isolated-hosting options for any system ingesting PHI in production. NobleCare is evaluating a VPC with strict egress controls and optional physical isolation for certification.
- Operational goal: get a pilot running with 50k inference requests/day, 95% P90 latency < 250ms, and a path to scale to 250k/day.

Networking & hosting constraints you flagged
- No outbound internet from compute nodes unless via a managed NAT with static IPs registered to NobleCare.
- Strict IP allowlist on your side; SFTP push/pull into a secured bucket is required for batch jobs.
- Option to host in a private datacenter (on-prem) if cloud residency gates cannot be cleared by MSA signing.

What Redwood can offer (high level)
- Private deployment (VPC) with a customer-controlled NAT and static egress IPs; optional on-prem package for air-gapped deployments.
- Audit logs and KMS integrations that meet SOC2+level evidence collection; we’ll map the audit artifacts to your checklist.
- Pilot blueprint: dedicated small GPU pool, prefix caching to reduce token cost, can meet the latency targets at pilot scale.

Agreed next steps (owner / ETA)
1) We (Soojin + Ben) will send a network checklist and an initial hosting decision matrix by EOD — Ben will own the networking checklist. (Today EOD)
2) NobleCare to confirm the set of public IPs you can accept for NAT egress or let us know if you require a customer-managed NAT appliance. (Tom / 3 business days)
3) Scheduling: technical deep-dive to validate TLS termination, outbound rules, and audit evidence — propose Thu 1 Jul 09:30 CEST. Please confirm. (All / confirm by Wed)
4) If on-prem required, we’ll scope SOW/estimation and a hardware checklist. (Soojin / follow-up after deep-dive)

Attachments: I’ve attached a stub checklist and a simple decision matrix for you to review.

Placeholder attachments: redwood-vpc-network-checklist.xlsx (network fields to fill), noblecare-hosting-decision-matrix.pdf

If I missed anything or misstated priorities, call it out and I’ll update.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +44 20 5555 1212

From: Dr. Emily Park <epark@noblecare.health>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <t.reyes@noblecare.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: NobleCare call — recap, constraints, and proposed next steps

Soojin — thanks for the detailed recap. Couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress / NAT: we cannot accept third-party-managed dynamic egress IPs. If Redwood can provide a managed NAT whose outbound IPs are fixed and registered to NobleCare, that is acceptable. Alternatively, we will deploy a customer-managed NAT appliance in our VPC and expect Redwood to route through it.

2) Data retention: 7 years retention is non-negotiable for audit logs tied to PHI access. We need to see a sample log schema to confirm compatibility.

3) Performance: pilot numbers are fine; we will provide representative load patterns in the network checklist.

We are OK to do the technical deep-dive on Thu 1 Jul 09:30 CEST — Tom will share the calendar invite. Please include someone from Infra/Networking (Ben is great).

Also — can you confirm whether your private deployment option supports HSM-backed key management (we require HSM for production)?

Best,
Emily
Dr. Emily Park
Chief Medical Information Officer, NobleCare

On Tue, 29 Jun 2027 at 13:02, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: NobleCare call — recap, constraints, and proposed next steps

Emily — great, thanks for the quick reply and the clear asks. Short responses inline below plus updated owners.

1) Egress / NAT — options
- Option A (preferred by Redwood): Redwood-managed static NAT IPs dedicated to NobleCare. We provide two static IPs per region, we register them in the brief and you add to your allowlist. Works well for hosted/private deployments.
- Option B (customer-managed): NobleCare deploys a single-customer NAT device; Redwood routes outbound through that appliance. This is supported in our Private deployment model but will add ~2–3 weeks to pilot setup depending on networking approvals.

Owner: Ben Carter to prepare the exact IP allocation and an architectural sketch for the Thu deep-dive.

2) HSM / KMS
- Redwood supports HSM-backed KMS for Private/on-prem installs via integrations with major KMS vendors (we also support customer-managed HSMs in on-prem packages). Ben will include a short artifact list showing HSM attestations and how keys are rotated.

Owner: Ben Carter — will attach sample log schema + KMS/HSM artifact list in the post-call packet.

3) Logs & retention
- We can map our audit events to your 7-year retention requirement; will propose storage tiers and export paths.

Owner: Laura Bennett — will outline retention tiers and compliance footprint; follow-up doc posted to the Drive link.

4) Deep-dive: Thu 1 Jul 09:30 CEST — Ben + Laura + Soojin will attend. Expect a 60–75m technical session. Please add the NobleCare infra contact to the invite.

Next deliverables (what you’ll receive before the deep-dive)
- Networking checklist (spreadsheet) — Ben (EOD today)
- IP allocation options + architecture sketch — Ben (before Thu deep-dive)
- Sample audit log schema + HSM/KMS artifact list — Ben (before Thu deep-dive)
- Retention/ export options doc — Laura (before Thu deep-dive)

Attachments referenced: redwood-vpc-network-checklist.xlsx, noblecare-hosting-decision-matrix.pdf

I’ll follow up with the Drive link and we’ll sync calendar invites. Looking forward to the session.

—
Soojin Lee
